source.title: Social cognition, joint attention, and communicative competence from 9 to 15 months of age.
source.venue: Monographs of the Society for Research in Child Development

confidence_rationale: Named anchor, verified. Monthly longitudinal study of 24 infants: social-cognitive skills emerged in an ordered sequence (sharing, following, directing attention) while nonsocial skills did not, and time in joint engagement plus maternal follow-in language predicted earliest gestural and linguistic communication. This is close to A1's structure (social milestones vs nonsocial controls) but n=24, correlational, and joint engagement is not the same construct as play maturation.
failure_signatures: Small sample (n=24) with many correlations; predictive relations may not replicate at scale.
Joint engagement is scaffolded largely by the mother; the predictor may be caregiver input rather than the infant's play competence.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Time infants spend in joint engagement with mothers, and mothers' language that follows into the infant's attentional focus, predict the earliest gestural and linguistic communication; social-cognitive skills emerge in a reliable sequence that nonsocial skills do not follow.
mapping.ree_translation: Supports MECH-308's claim that language onset is anchored in shared-frame social interaction (basic-expression channels such as mutual gaze and pointing), and partially instantiates A1: social milestones, unlike nonsocial ones, are ordered and linked to communication.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Joint attentional engagement (often around toys) overlaps with but is not play_mode in MECH-308's sense (frame opening/closing, synthetic goals, bracketed consequences). The nonsocial comparison skills were cognitive (e.g. object tasks), not the motor/sensory milestones A1 specifies. No causal manipulation.
mapping.source_context: Longitudinal monthly visits 9-15 months, typically developing infants; PubMed record has no DOI.

confidence_components.notes: Anchor named in claim note; verified via PubMed.
